FR-001.title: The public-access settings window MUST show the saved player login as read-only summary information rather than an inline editing field.

FR-002.title: When a saved player password is present, the settings window MUST display exactly ***** regardless of the password's actual length.

FR-003.title: When a saved player password is absent or unavailable, the settings window MUST communicate that state without displaying the fixed mask.

FR-004.title: Player-login editing MUST occur in a dedicated modal dialog patterned after the existing ngrok token dialog.

FR-005.title: The player-credential dialog MUST support replacing the login and password together, changing the login while preserving an existing password, deleting the saved credential pair, and cancelling without mutation.

FR-006.title: Deleting saved player credentials MUST remove the saved password and restore the default player login.

FR-007.title: Every credential-dialog close path MUST clear transient password values and restore focus appropriately.

FR-008.title: The settings window MUST provide one Share action that is enabled only when a valid saved login and password are available.

FR-009.title: The Share action MUST copy one readable value containing both the saved login and saved password.

FR-010.title: The saved password MUST be read only inside a bounded trusted operation that writes the clipboard, clears temporary buffers, and returns only success or a safe error to the page.

FR-011.title: The implementation MUST preserve active-access confirmation, stale-snapshot suppression, generated-password handling, credential validation, and local/LAN failure isolation.

FR-012.title: Automated checks MUST cover fixed masking, configured and unconfigured dialogs, replacement, preservation, deletion, cancellation, sharing success, and secure-store or clipboard failure.

context: area: public-access native service, Overseer settings UI, generated bindings, and browser fixtures
constraint: saved password mask is exactly *****
constraint: Go changes follow repository cleanup and validation rules
intent: Let game masters safely manage and share saved player login credentials from public-access settings.
expectations: ngrok token management, domain configuration, and explicit public-access lifecycle behavior remain unchanged
approach: Move player credential editing into a focused dialog and add a native one-shot share command that writes the scoped secure password directly to the clipboard without returning it to the browser.

decisions.decision: Write saved player credentials to the clipboard inside the native boundary
decisions.why: The page receives no stored password while the requested one-click share flow remains possible
decisions.rejected: Returning the password through a desktop result for JavaScript clipboard handling

decisions.decision: Manage login and password as one child-dialog unit
decisions.why: They form one Basic Auth credential pair and match the established token-management interaction
decisions.rejected: Leaving login editing inline while moving only password editing

decisions.decision: Reuse CommandResult and avoid protobuf changes
decisions.why: Sharing is a private native side effect with no reusable data payload
decisions.rejected: Adding a serializable secret-bearing credential response

plan.summary: Designed a native clipboard share boundary plus focused player-credential dialog across existing public-access layers
plan.key_finding: The Wails host already exposes an injectable ClipboardManager, so the saved password never needs to enter JavaScript

tasks.summary: 14 tasks across native secret handling, three user-story phases, and final verification with explicit dependency waves

implement.summary: Implemented and verified fixed saved-password masking, focused credential management, and native login/password sharing without exposing the password to JavaScript
implement.key_finding: The password remains inside a scoped secure-store callback and the Wails clipboard boundary; desktop results carry only success or safe error state
implement.risks: Clipboard contents are intentionally readable by the operating system after an explicit Share action
